title: CS1-BACKWARD: terminal seed and backward two-candidate phase decoder

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and fixed hidden shift s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2 N), use exactly the single CS1-BACKWARD configuration in the complete evidence proof. It receives only fresh independent ideal mixed coset copies and recovers the full s with unconditional success at least1-2^-8>2/3. For n>=64 and odd part M>1, use the unchanged TREE_d with R=nq_d, ell=ceil(log2 R), terminal H=ceil(log2 M), seed stages u=0,...,ell+3 at physical scales H+u, K_seed=8192(ell+ceil(log2 n)+30), followed by H backward two-candidate steps using K_back=512(ceil(log2 n)+30) roots each. The odd root count is F=(ell+4)K_seed+H K_back. For M=1 skip it and set F=0. Use K2=ceil(log2 n)+30 attempts per 2-adic bit; Qcap=1024[6*2^mu_star*(kappa_star+1)*(F+2a2)+2a2], and recompute the Section5 extractor/fallback parameters with that cap. The finite n<64 algorithm is explicitly specified. Every bound holds jointly on every branch, including all wrong labels, rejections, discarded trees, retries and aborts, with absolute constants independent of N,s and outcomes. Total charged work is O(n^(7/2)(log2 n)^2 2^(sqrt(2n))) and hence O(n^(7/2)(log2 n)^2 2^(a sqrt n)), with the exact rational a=u_333/v_333 defined by the proof recurrence and identical to the material predecessor. All uniform compilation, gate generation, address work, exact arithmetic, initialization, measurements and source costs are included. The full representative structured envelope has exact growth index1/2.
